answer:
**Mixed umbrella (ETF and non-ETF sub-funds):** The umbrella name need not include "UCITS ETF". Each ETF sub-fund must carry the identifier in its name, prospectus/supplement, KID and marketing communications. Non-ETF sub-funds must not use it, and documents should clearly separate the two.

**Sub-fund with listed and unlisted classes:** The Central Bank of Ireland permits ETF status at share-class level. The identifier then goes in the **names of the listed (ETF) classes**, not the sub-fund name, so unlisted classes aren't described as ETFs. The supplement should state which classes are ETF classes and explain dealing differences, such as primary-market access versus direct subscription and redemption.

**Key point:** An all-ETF sub-fund is identified at sub-fund level. A mixed sub-fund is identified at class level. Non-ETF siblings, whether sub-funds or classes, are never labelled "UCITS ETF".

Check the latest CBI UCITS Q&A for current wording.
